Title: W722 - Longbridge Weir Hydroelectric Plant Maintenance
Description:
The Longbridge Weir Hydropower House was constructed in 2011 to generate renewable electricity, primarily for the Council House. Derwent Hydroelectric Power Ltd was the original designer and constructor of the installation and has provided operation and maintenance services since commissioning.

The plant has now been operational for approximately 14 years. As it approaches the later stages of its asset lifecycle, several major components are at increased risk of failure due to age and will require replacement within the next five years. Ongoing operation and maintenance therefore require specialist technical knowledge of
the original design and construction of the installation.

Accordingly, a direct award is permitted under the Procurement Act 2023, Schedule 5, item 6(a), as competition is absent for technical reasons and only a particular supplier can supply the required
services. The market for contractors capable of maintaining and upgrading a small-scale hydropower installation of this nature is extremely limited. The plant requires a cost-effective 24-hour emergency response capability, which most specialist providers are unable to deliver. Derwent Hydroelectric Power Ltd is locally based, enabling this requirement to be met. As the original constructor, the supplier also has detailed and unique knowledge of the plant, presenting a significant technical barrier to alternative providers. The small scale of the installation further reduces commercial viability for other contractors. These market conditions are not expected to change.

Title: Free Breakfast Club Programme Food Partnering Open Call - Academic Year 26/27
Description:
The free breakfast club programme is one of the Department for Education's flagship policies, central to the Government's mission to break down barriers to opportunity for every child. Once fully implemented, it will deliver a free breakfast club in every primary school in England, giving millions of children the chance to start the day supported and ready to learn. 
 
Evidence shows that where schools run breakfast clubs, they report improvements to pupils' behaviour, attendance and attainment. The free breakfast club programme will mean every school, every child, and every family has the chance to receive those benefits.  

Since April 2025, we have funded c.750 schools to offer a free breakfast club as early adopters, delivering 7 million meals so far. Following the success of the early adopters, we are moving to national rollout investing a further £80m into the programme to fund an additional c.2,000 schools between April 2026 and March 2027. This will benefit around half a million more children. We invited schools with a 40% or higher Free School Meal (FSM) rate (or the most disadvantaged school in an area, whichever is lower) to apply to join the scheme in April 2026, getting the benefits to those who need them most, first. National rollout will then continue in September 2026, when more schools will open their free breakfast clubs, taking the total to c.3000 schools.  

Business Collaboration 

Through the free breakfast club programme, schools are fully funded to deliver a 30-minute club each morning, giving parents free childcare whilst their children can enjoy a nutritious breakfast, however, there is room to increase the impact so children can start their day in the best possible way. We know there are already great partnerships happening locally between schools, businesses and industry. The Department is keen to explore how we could strengthen and scale these approaches nationally, to maximise impact and enable all participating schools to benefit in the same way.  

During the early adopter 'test and learn' phase, the Department partnered with organisations across industry to further strengthen the programme's impact and maximise schools' funding, with a particular focus on breakfast provision. Following an Open Call published in July 2025, we received four offers of varied discounts/deals from national supermarkets and charities. These offers have been available to our c.750 early adopter schools since November 2025 and have been extremely well received by participating schools.  

As the rollout of free breakfast club continues, we want to build on the success of the early adopter phase by continuing to partner with organisations across the industry to help maximise the support available to schools.
Region: North East,North West,Yorkshire and The Humber,East Midlands,West Midlands,East of England,London,South East,South West

Additional Text:
We are seeking offers from food providers that enable  Participating Schools in the free breakfast club programme in the 2026/27 academic year to maximise the value of their food spending and enhance their breakfast provision for pupils. In return, the Department proposes to offer partners a package of rights, as detailed below. Any deals offered by the partner will not be mandated for Participating Schools to make use of and Participating Schools will retain flexibility and choice in how they procure their food. 

We know that Participating Schools source food for their free breakfast clubs from a wide range of food providers. This sponsorship is intended to leverage the profile of the programme at a national level to ensure all Participating Schools have access to the best value-for-money deals. We are also seeking to address challenges that Participating Schools face in ordering food, including ease of access and use of ordering systems, reliability of delivery, minimum order values and volume restrictions.

Organisation Name: ROYAL SOCIETY FOR THE PROTECTION OF BIRDS
Title: Downs to the Sea and Improving Pulborough and Amberley Projects at RSPB Amberley Wildbrooks
Description:
RSPB Amberley Wildbrooks is a large wetland reserve located in West Sussex. It sits within the South Downs National Park and is part of the Arun Valley. The majority of the reserve is made up of wetland which is designated SSSI, SPA, SAC and Ramsar. The wetland is important for both wintering waders and wildfowl and breeding birds such as Lapwing and Redshank.

Over the last 10 years, infrastructure on the site has been gradually declining. With the added pressure on increases in winter flood events and pressure form Fallow Deer, this decline has been rapid in recent years. The Downs to the Sea and Improving Pulborough and Amberley projects aim to restore the wetlands. Work to culverts will improve access and hydrological control. This will allow better grazing and control of water. Installation of a corral and new fencing will allow better grazing and reprofiling ditches where Anisus vorticulus are found will enhance habitat for this rare snail.

This work will help make the site more resilient to the wetter winters and drier summers we are seeing as a result of climate change. Wet features and scrapes will help hold water during drier times and replacing broken culverts will create better water flow and control.

Downs to the Sea has been established as a multi-partner project, led by the South Downs National Park Authority, to tackle these issues with the aim of helping to restore and protect crucial ponds and wetlands that are instrumental in nature recovery and resilience to climate change at scale, providing multiple ecosystem services: water for homes and farms, flood storage, wildlife habitat and recreation.  

The project will also connect with underserved audiences and those most vulnerable to health and wellbeing problems in the area and leave a legacy that highlights and supports the need for recovery and resilience in our communities, for both people and nature.   

The RSPB projects included in Downs to the Sea will see vital restoration works on a string of functionally connected nature reserves down through the Arun Valley. Work will focus on improving lowland wet grassland across the RSPB sites to benefit RSPB priority species (breeding waders and wintering wildfowl).

Title: Sizewell C - HR Monitoring (CRX & Building) Package
Description:
Overview of Scope 
      
      Supply and installation of the HR Monitoring System to the to CRX and Nuclear Island Building 
      
      The EAU (containment monitoring) system is required to continuously monitor and assess the mechanical behaviour and integrity of the Reactor Building and integrity of the Reactor Building and associated at nuclear island at Sizewell C (SZC) throughout construction, testing, and operation. The system scope covers the design, supply, installation, commissioning, and documentation of:
      •	Monitoring sensors (including extensometers, temperature probes, hydraulic levelling pots, pendulums, invar wires, inclinometers, hygrometers, and pressure sensors)
      •	Associated cabling, connection/grouping boxes, and acquisition/data logger cabinets
      •	All necessary software interfaces and data collection/reporting tools
      More than 200 sensors will be embedded and installed in both the inner containment wall and the common raft of the nuclear island.
      The EAU monitoring system must provide real-time and periodic data on:
      •	Settlements and deformations of the nuclear island raft (topographical markers, hydraulic levelling pots, extensometers, and temperature sensors)
      •	Overall containment distortions (pendulums and invar wires)
      •	Localized deformations and tendon failure detection (embedded extensometers, local monitoring devices)
      •	Tension in prestressed cables (dynamometers)
      •	Environmental parameters (temperature, humidity, internal and external pressure)
      All EAU system components must comply with the Book of Technical Specifications (BTS) Chapter 9.04 and associated referenced as well as client installation and interface requirements. Instruments must be delivered with calibration certificates and installed in accordance with manufacturer and project-specific procedures.
      The EAU system contractor will also provide:
      •	Installation studies and execution drawings for all phases (temporary/erection and permanent/operational)
      •	Material Approval Forms, Inspection and Test Plans, Quality Release Certificates, and Lifetime Quality Records (LTQR)
      •	Data collection, reporting formats, and periodic analysis files as required by the client (monthly/bi-monthly during construction; weekly/daily during key phases; and as specified during operation)

Title: Principal and General Bridge Inspections 2026 - 2031
Description:
Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust (The Customer) requires a Supplier for provision of bridge inspections including, but not limited to, principal and general inspections.

Bridge inspections are systematic, legally mandated, and safety-critical evaluations of bridge structures to identify defects, monitor deterioration (such as corrosion or cracks), and assess structural integrity. For example, if a problem in a bridge is not detected early, it could eventually lead to a catastrophic incident, such as a bridge failure or a complete collapse of the bridge, resulting in serious injury or even death.

The prime focus of all bridge inspection is public safety and prolonging economic life of structure. The assessment includes an assessment of the load carrying capacity of all bridges which is required to determine if fire services can use bridges in an emergency, for example.

The purpose of the contract is to assess the load carrying capability of bridges at the Customer's Premises and Locations to enable it to satisfy relevant statutory requirement. The objective is to ensure its bridges are safe for use by the Customer's staff, patients and members of the public.

Principal inspections are required every 6 years. This level of inspection requires a close examination (within touching distance) of all necessary parts of structure, including access equipment and non-destructible testing.

The scope of the contract may increase to include bridges at additional Premises and Locations throughout the Term.

The contract has been procured via Lot 8d (Health and Safety) of the ESPO 664_25 (Consultancy Services) Framework: https://www.espo.org/consultancy-services-664-25.html
